questions: Does the baseline reproduce 20/20 oval finishes at about 1.65 s, confirming the platform is stable and repeatable?
On the s-bend and slalom, at which track position and progress does the first line loss start, and what is the lateral error at that step?
At the first line loss, do the outer sensors read near 1 or near 0, and is the loss on the inside or outside of the bend?

intent: Reproduce the iteration-0 baseline exactly, with no geometry changed, to restore the best-scoring stable platform (score 356.6, oval 20/20 at about 1.65 s). The Integrator should use the fixed platform to report, per bend, the progress and lateral error at first line loss on the s-bend and slalom, and the sensor readings at that step. This tells us whether the bend limit is sensor-geometric or controller-side. Expected result: oval finishes near 20/20 and a score near 356.
learning: Nine iterations show the platform is a sharp local optimum: every change from the iteration-0 baseline has either collapsed the oval or cut its finish rate. Geometry alone has not moved the s-bend or slalom beyond progress 0.28, so the bend limit is probably controller-side or a deeper geometry issue that a single lever cannot reach. Future proposals should keep the baseline as the reference and change only one variable at a time, and should not treat a bend gain under an oval collapse as a real improvement.
rationale: The evidence across nine iterations points to a sharp local optimum at the iteration-0 baseline. It is the only design that finishes any track: 20/20 on the oval at about 1.65 s, scoring 356.6 overall. Every single-variable or combined change since then has either collapsed the oval to 0/20 or cut finishes (iteration 1 to 17/20, iteration 2 to 15/20). That covers the sensor lead at y=0.03 and y=0.07 m, footprints of 8 and 16 mm, the wider ±0.032 m array (iteration 7 collapsed the oval, which overturns the iteration-2 bend-gain reading), and body length 0.12 m (iteration 8, scored 78.4, oval 0/20). The s-bend and slalom have never moved meaningfully above progress 0.28 and 0.12, so no geometry tested so far fixes them. The remaining levers are small, and any change risks the one stable configuration. The final evaluation runs on an unseen track of a different shape, so a reproducible, robust platform is worth more than a speculative bend gain. I therefore revert to the iteration-0 baseline exactly. This secures the proven oval finish and the best known score, and it gives the Integrator a fixed platform to diagnose where the s-bend and slalom fail (the step and lateral error at first line loss, and the sensor readings at that step). I expect a score near 356, matching the baseline's seed-stable oval result. No bend completion is expected from geometry alone.
